verification_candidates.claim_text: Antioxidant supplements have no evidence that they do anything.

verification_candidates.rationale: The claim that antioxidant supplements lack benefit is checkable against trials and reviews.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Resveratrol is not really absorbed; blood levels spike for roughly 30 minutes and then it is excreted or converted into another compound.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: all of the studies on resveratrol, since the 1990s have found, you don't really absorb it, you get a spike of it for roughly 30 minutes
verification_candidates.rationale: Resveratrol pharmacokinetics are checkable, and this claim undermines the red-wine health narrative.

verification_candidates.evidence_quote: You're not able to get the amount of resveratrol that would give you any kind of benefit
verification_candidates.rationale: Whether any achievable resveratrol dose has benefit is checkable and material to supplement and wine claims.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The only real evidence that resveratrol could be isolated and have health effects comes from studies of yeast, fruit flies and mice.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: the only real evidence that resveratrol could be isolated and could have these health effects is on studies of yeast, fruit flies and mice
verification_candidates.rationale: The state of the human evidence for resveratrol can be checked.
